beyondthehorizon.options.title: Beyond the Terrain Settings
beyondthehorizon.options.enabled.tooltip: Draws terrain beyond the render distance. Needs the mod on the server too (singleplayer: the client is enough).
beyondthehorizon.options.distance.toolti: How far the terrain is drawn, in chunks (24 - 10000). Type a number. The fog ends at this distance.
beyondthehorizon.options.sharpness.toolt: How far out finer tiles are used. Higher is sharper and slower.
beyondthehorizon.options.start_level.too: Blocks per cell of the finest tiles. Larger is faster, smaller is sharper near the render distance.
beyondthehorizon.options.max_tiles.toolt: Most pieces (tiles) of the distant terrain kept in graphics memory at once. Lower it if memory runs out, raise it if far terrain reloads as you move.
beyondthehorizon.options.fog_mode.toolti: Whose fog the terrain has at the end of the view.
beyondthehorizon.options.fog_start.toolt: Where the fog starts, in percent of where it ends.
beyondthehorizon.options.water_fog.toolt: Whether the terrain has the fog of water when seen from under it.
beyondthehorizon.options.tree_level.tool: Approximated trees on the finest tiles, up to this terrain sample spacing. They are not the real trees. Applies to tiles loaded after the change: rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.options.tree_density.to: How many trees there are, in percent of the default. Applies to tiles loaded after the change.
beyondthehorizon.options.step_level.tool: Tiles with a terrain sample spacing up to this are drawn as stepped columns of the heightmap (flat tops, walls between them), like blocks, instead of the smooth ground. Applies to tiles loaded after the change: rejoin the world.
From this terrain sample spacing on, trees are flat sprites (your own textures) instead of boxes: cheaper and closer to how trees look from afar. Applies to tiles loaded after the change: rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.options.pixel_filter.to: Pixelates the ground colors: the smooth blend is read on a grid 2, 4 or 8 times finer than the terrain samples, with a little noise for a textured look.
beyondthehorizon.options.server_settings: The settings of the tile server of this world (beyond-the-terrain-server.json).
Only available in a singleplayer world. A dedicated server is set up in its beyond-the-terrain-server.json.
beyondthehorizon.server.title: Beyond the Terrain Server Settings
beyondthehorizon.server.rejoin: Beyond the Terrain: server settings saved. Threads, priority and caches apply when you rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.generator_thread: Threads that generate the distant terrain. Auto uses all cores but one, at least two. Applies when you rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.generator_priori: Java priority of the generator threads, 1 (lowest) to 9. Higher gets more CPU time against the game, chunk generation and other mods. They still pause for late frames. Applies when you rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.in_flight_per_th: Tiles handed to the generator for each thread before it reports back. More keeps the threads busy when the server thread is late, fewer reacts faster when you move. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.max_in_flight.to: The least number of tiles a player may have in flight. The setting per thread raises it when it gives more. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.max_queued.toolt: How many tile requests of one player wait on the server. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.min_level.toolti: The finest tile level the server generates. Higher levels are coarser and faster. Players learn it when they rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.max_distance.too: How far from a player the server generates distant terrain, in steps of 1 000 blocks. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.enabled.tooltip: Turns the distant terrain of this server on or off. Players learn it when they rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.builds.tooltip: Where the real world is known (explored chunks), villages, other structures and what players built are drawn as part of the distant terrain, as stepped columns that guess their look from the heights and the block colors. Off, they are left out and the generated terrain shows. Applies at once; players see it for tiles they load again, or after clearing the terrain cache.
beyondthehorizon.server.builds_level.too: The biggest tiles that still show builds, apart from the terrain quality: a tile is 32 blocks wide at the finest level, so builds are drawn near the explored world and fade out into plain terrain farther away. Higher shows them farther, at a cost in generation. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.pregen_threads.t: Generator threads while terrain is generated ahead by /farplane pregen distant. Auto uses all cores but one. Applies when the next generation starts.
beyondthehorizon.server.disk_cache.toolt: Keeps generated tiles in the world folder, so the next visit loads them instead of generating them. Applies when you rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.memory_cache.too: Tiles kept in the memory of the server. Applies when you rejoin the world.
